opening.text: There was a boy called Theo who looked after the frog pond at his school.
Theo counted the frogs, cleared fallen leaves and listened to them croak in the clear water.
After a big storm, the pond turned brown with mud and bits of leaves. "The frogs need clean water," said Theo, "and there's no money for a pump!"

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. A storm has turned Theo's frog pond brown, and there's no money for a pump. Can you help him make the water clear again? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea for cleaning dirty water. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been filtering water for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who make water clean!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which material will make the muddy water clearest?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your filter cut in half, like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your filter and pour 250 ml of muddy water through it. This water is for frogs and plants only, never for drinking!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change the order of your layers and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, YOUR filter keeps Theo's pond clear, and the frogs croak happily all summer long!

quick_check.question: One oyster can filter up to 50 litres of water a day. How much could 2 oysters filter?
quick_check.right: Right! 50 + 50 = 100 litres a day. A whole oyster reef can clean a huge bay!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Try 50 litres plus another 50 litres.

clue_cards.name: Oyster
clue_cards.trick: It pulls water over its gills, where sticky mucus traps tiny bits.
clue_cards.does: One oyster can filter up to 50 litres of water a day.

clue_cards.name: Baleen whale
clue_cards.trick: It pushes seawater out through bristly plates called baleen.
clue_cards.does: The water flows out, and the krill stay trapped inside.

clue_cards.name: Mangroves
clue_cards.trick: Their tangled roots, like marsh plants, slow river water down.
clue_cards.does: Mud and dirt sink to the bottom before the water reaches the sea.

clue_cards.name: Soil and sand
clue_cards.trick: Rainwater trickles slowly down through their layers.
clue_cards.does: It comes out clean in underground rivers.

predict.prompt: Gets clearer or clogs up? Predict first!

items.label: A paper filter on top, taking all the mud
Muddy water left to stand still

predict.explain: Coarse gaps first catch the big bits, then finer ones catch the small bits. If the fine layer comes first, it clogs straight away. Still water lets heavy mud settle on its own.

lab.title: The mud lab
lab.predict: Pour equal amounts of muddy water through each one. Which will come out clearest?

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: You already know the first 3 whys. Today you'll learn all 5 and dig right down to the root cause of a problem.

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 🚪 Why does it squeak? The hinge rubs.
parts.starter: Why is the pond murky? Because…

parts.name: Why #2
parts.example: 🚪 Why does it rub? The hinge is dry.
parts.starter: Why is there so much mud in the water? Because…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 🚪 Why is it dry? The oil wore off.
parts.starter: Why did the storm wash mud in? Because…

parts.name: Why #4
parts.example: 🚪 Why? Nobody oiled it for years.
parts.starter: Why is the ground near the pond so muddy? Because…

parts.name: Why #5
parts.what: Find the root cause, then fix that.
parts.example: 🚪 Why? No one knew. Fix: an oiling reminder!
parts.starter: Why does nothing stop the mud getting in? Because…
